102-1: The 102nd term begins with Megumi Fujishima, a former child star forced into Hasunosora's boarding school, arriving disdainful of the entrance ceremony and stiff freshman rep Kozue Otomune. She meets the enigmatic Tsuzuri Yugiri, who enrolled solely to become a school idol, and is cornered by Sachi Ogami, the club's lone second-year, who drags her to meet Kozue. A clash erupts between Megumi's professional pride and Kozue's Love Live! devotion, though Tsuzuri impresses everyone as a dance prodigy. After a vulnerable bath conversation and an all-night school idol video marathon, the trio begins to bond, and Sachi gleefully watches her 'problem children' come together, marking the chaotic birth of the trio later nicknamed the Hasu no Daisankaku (Great Triangle).
102-2: A week into the club, Megumi grows increasingly drawn to the eccentric Tsuzuri, even as she keeps bickering with Kozue, and realizes Tsuzuri carries a deep sadness she calls 'rain in her heart' that never stops. Sachi announces a late-April live at the Music Hall; Kozue protests the three-week prep time, but Sachi insists showing the growth process is what being a school idol means, then unveils Hasunosora's three traditional units: Cerise Bouquet, DOLLCHESTRA, and Mira-Cra Park!. To the freshmen's shock, Sachi reveals she has already partnered with Tsuzuri to form DOLLCHESTRA, and since Kozue and Megumi refuse to work together, Sachi proposes joining both their units herself as a temporary bridge so the club can field all three.
102-3: Kozue reflects on how she dreamed of Love Live! since first grade and fought her prestigious musical family to attend Hasunosora, even as she grows frustrated watching Megumi's casual popularity at school. During practice Sachi trains all three units at once, revealing she is the chairwoman's granddaughter and a prodigy in her own right, but the tension peaks when Megumi suddenly stops coming. Kozue discovers Megumi watched her old TV show and realized the audience has moved on and forgotten her; devastated by the fleeting nature of fame, Megumi decides to quit the club and chase her old career, calling school idols a waste of time. Until Kozue confronts her in the dorm, arguing that their bond matters more than any industry comeback.
102-4: On the day of the April debut, Sachi surprises the club with replica costumes of the legendary Dream Believers who once won Love Live!, moving Kozue to tears while Megumi stays cynical before admitting the quality. Tsuzuri stuns everyone with her natural stage presence at the Music Hall, where DOLLCHESTRA performs 'Sparkly Spot' and Megumi watches Sachi and Tsuzuri grow into a real unit. As Kozue's solo 'Reflection in the Mirror' approaches, Megumi feels creeping anxiety, but when Kozue freezes on stage, Megumi's support and the trio's trust pull her through, proving to Megumi that school idols can truly be the 'light' Kozue always believed in.
102-5: By mid-May Megumi has settled into the club, growing close to Tsuzuri (who now calls her 'Megu') and dropping honorifics with Kozue ('Kozu'). Recognizing her TV background, Sachi pushes her onto School Idol Connect (Suku-Cone) streaming; though Megumi mocks the low production, she finds her niche in casual 'zatsudan' talk streams and realizes broadcasting is a weapon to stand out from her polished peers. As the club preps for June's Nadeshiko Festival, Megumi's streaming confidence grows, and she begins bridging her old celebrity instincts with the amateur warmth of school idol culture.
102-6: In mid-June the Nadeshiko Festival prep consumes the club, with Megumi and Kozue developing a morning ritual to wake the oversleeping Tsuzuri. After Kozue's late-May birthday she has softened into a sisterly caretaker for Tsuzuri while Megumi handles her styling, and in the clubroom Kozue finally unveils the original song she has been composing, a 'beginning song' for the three of them. They divide the work (Tsuzuri choreography, Megumi costumes, Kozue music), with Megumi pushing modern casual looks against Kozue's competitive artistic pride, setting the stage for their festival performance.
102-7: With a week left, rehearsals for Kozue's new song crack under the weight of Tsuzuri's brilliant but near-impossible choreography, and Megumi snaps at both friends before storming out. Tsuzuri follows with hot cocoa, mirroring a kindness Megumi once showed her, and tearfully offers to dumb down the choreography, but Megumi clarifies her anger comes from her own insecurity, not Tsuzuri's talent, and refuses to let her apologize. Returning to the lesson room, Megumi sincerely apologizes to Kozue, and the three commit to performing the piece exactly as planned, their bond stronger for the fracture.
103-1: Kaho Hinoshita, raised sickly and overprotected, arrives at Hasunosora bursting with dreams of freedom but finds the secluded campus and cold bus-mate Sayaka crushing her spirit. Rescued from a school otter by Kozue, she is dragged to watch the School Idol Club perform with Tsuzuri, an experience that awakens Sayaka's desire to join. Kozue recruits Kaho as logistics manager for the upcoming Welcome Live. As the transfer deadline looms, Kozue shares how her own musical family opposed her dream and urges Kaho to find her own reason to bloom. Kaho tears up her transfer application, officially joins the club, and performs at the Welcome Live alongside Kozue, finally claiming her place at Hasunosora.
103-2: After formally joining, Kaho throws herself into a week of daily courtyard lives, discovering a natural talent for streaming on the School Idol Connect app that even motivates her classmates to join the choir. Sayaka introduces her to the app and Tsuzuri helps register her, but when Kaho watches her own performance archives and sees how far she lags behind Kozue and the already-famous Sayaka, she suffers a total loss of confidence and breaks down. Kozue reassures her that her raw passion and 'straightforward feelings' are her greatest strength and shares her philosophy that school idols inspire by showing their effort trajectory; Kaho requests Kozue's strict training and publicly declares her goal to become the world's best school idol. Kozue also reveals the club's past as the former Performing Arts Club and confirms Kaho will form a unit with her, not Tsuzuri.
103-3: Kozue sets an ambitious goal, first place at an upcoming city-wide school idol event, and puts Kaho through a grueling training regimen based on her own middle-school routine, confiscating Kaho's manga as motivation. Pushed too hard, Kaho secretly practices at night, strains her leg, and lies about it at the live; when she falls backstage, Kozue is injured shielding her, and Megumi Fujishima appears to encourage Kaho. Ashamed, Kaho confesses her dishonesty, and after Sayaka reframes her 'selfishness' as sincere effort, Kaho discovers the legacy 'School Idol Notebooks,' reads Kozue's private entries revealing how happy mentoring makes her, and reconciles with Kozue in the Big Warehouse. The two officially form Cerise Bouquet, debut at their live, win April's Monthly MVP, and Megumi, now on hiatus, streams an intro praising Kaho's 'sun-like' spirit.
103-4: While Kaho and Kozue shine, Sayaka grows insecure about her own progress, even as Tsuzuri, grateful for Sayaka's bentos and wake-up care, struggles to wake herself. Kozue warns Sayaka about the difficulty of partnering the genius Tsuzuri, whose spontaneous hallway dance is broken up by Sachi; when Tsuzuri rejects a school-tour offer to focus on Sayaka, Sayaka leaves feeling inadequate. Kozue confronts Tsuzuri about her poor communication, and a flashback reveals Tsuzuri scouted Sayaka by performing on the spot and calling her a 'great school idol,' the foundation of Sayaka's motivation. In the present Tsuzuri admits she was wrong to stop communicating and confesses she doesn't even consider herself a 'school idol,' just a solitary artist; Sayaka validates Tsuzuri's identity and they officially agree to be school idols together, closing a successful live with a lighthearted oden plan.
103-5: Tsuzuri gives Kaho and Kozue acorns as thanks for helping her realize she'd neglected Sayaka, then during DOLLCHESTRA practice she critiques Sayaka's lack of 'presence,' pushing Sayaka to open up about her struggles. Sayaka reveals her sister's career-ending injury and her own fear of inadequacy, so Tsuzuri drags her to a Kanazawa market to work at a seafood bowl shop run by acquaintance Reika. Sayaka initially fails to greet customers with warmth, but Reika explains Tsuzuri's role is simply being a 'billboard' whose presence makes people happy, triggering Sayaka's realization that she must reciprocate the community's support. She delivers a high-energy greeting, impresses Kaho (who streams it), and learns the senior-junior market tradition Tsuzuri insisted she experience, finally accepting her own identity over imitating her sister and resolving to decide her future.
103-6: Sayaka wakes with renewed purpose as Tsuzuri suggests she lead choreography and names her color 'light blue.' At the rink with Kaho, Sayaka reveals her skating was inspired by her sister, and her former rival Tsukasa retires, releasing Sayaka from skating only for her sake. When Tsuzuri plans to sacrifice the club's live for Tsukasa's farewell show, Kaho helps Sayaka see both act from love. Sayaka performs incorporating her school-idol growth, pulls Tsuzuri into an impromptu live, and they name their unit DOLLCHESTRA, while across the ocean Rurino begins her own journey toward Hasunosora.
103-7: Kaho and Sayaka write the club's introductory article for the Nadeshiko Festival, learning to focus on the club's true appeal. Their work is upended when Rurino Osawa, Megumi's childhood friend just back from California, bursts in to join, captivated by their livestream. Kaho and Sayaka separately visit Kozue and Tsuzuri to propose a four-person performance. Kozue and Tsuzuri, who swore never to perform together again after last year's Love Live! failure, accept and choose Tsuzuri's 'revenge' song. The club trains together as the juniors vow to help the seniors finally conquer the piece that once defeated them.
103-8: As Nadeshiko Festival prep intensifies, Kozue and Tsuzuri model the difficult revenge choreography, Kozue admitting her old regret at never matching Tsuzuri's level; Kaho and Sayaka throw their full support behind the seniors. The festival live succeeds, and in its glow the six members debut as a unified four-unit-ready club, bonding over shared relief. Megumi, still physically healed but psychologically blocked from dancing after her stage fall, watches from the sidelines, proud yet distant, while Rurino begins to sense something is wrong with her childhood friend who invited her to be a school idol but now avoids the stage entirely.
103-9: Rurino formally joins and quickly becomes the club's energetic spark, but she grows confused that Megumi, who first inspired her, has gone distant and stopped visiting. Kozue and Tsuzuri finally reveal the truth: at last year's Rindou Festival, Megumi fell and was injured; though her body healed, the trauma left a psychological block where her legs freeze on stage, so she quit performing and turned to video production. Determined to help, Rurino leads Kaho and Sayaka to Megumi's dorm, but Megumi greets them warmly yet deflects, claiming exhaustion from editing and gently turning them away, leaving Rurino hurt and more resolved to reach her.
103-10: Rurino shares Megumi's 'Halo-Megu!' videos, and the first-years learn Megumi is the same girl they saw at the festival and visiting Kozue in hospital; Kozue and Tsuzuri explain Megumi's injury and stage fright. Rurino drags Kaho and Sayaka to confront her, but Megumi keeps her distance behind a tired-editor facade. Undeterred, Rurino declares she'll bring Megumi back to the stage herself, and the club begins scheming how to reconnect their lost senpai, setting up the emotional core of the term as friendship pushes against fear.
103-11: With all three units active, Kozue plans a large Kanazawa live, but Megumi returns to the club frustrated by the members' lax discipline: Sayaka and Tsuzuri distracted by clouds, Kaho lost in manga, Rurino out of 'battery.' Kozue's gentle, grandmotherly leniency surprises Megumi, who decides to enforce professionalism herself. She engineers a 'working retreat' at a hot-spring inn framed as a productivity contest, but her hospitality tricks are upstaged when Cerise Bouquet and DOLLCHESTRA excel through genuine effort; the ruse is exposed when the others overhear her plan. Still, the trip yields a successful mini-live, and a promo video Megumi edits overnight goes viral, suddenly thrusting the club into the spotlight and forcing everyone to grow into their new visibility.
103-12: Sayaka, Kaho, and Rurino promote the Rindo Festival, Kozue framing it as the club's 'revenge' performance and their official Love Live! district-qualifier video entry. She explains qualifiers run on submitted videos due to the huge field, and wants all three units, Cerise Bouquet, DOLLCHESTRA, and Mira-Cra Park!, to pass. As they prepare, Kozue privately revisits the sapling certificate, the non-interference pact she, Tsuzuri, and Megumi signed after Megumi's injury and Sachi's departure; rejecting blame, the second-years reconcile into the Hasu no Daisankaku (Great Triangle) and submit a six-member entry. But Kozue overworks herself and collapses, Sayaka steps in as acting president, and she, Kaho, and Rurino hit a wall with the student council over a stage permit, turning the festival push into a fight on two fronts.
103-13: The club celebrates passing the Love Live! district qualifiers, and Tsuzuri, happy the group is whole, feels urgency not to be left behind as Sayaka shines handling admin for both DOLLCHESTRA and Mira-Cra Park!. Impulsively she volunteers for the Open Campus committee, leading it with singing and dancing despite initial anxiety and Sayaka's loneliness at her distance. When a rainstorm leads Sachi to consider canceling the finale, Tsuzuri confronts her lingering trauma over Sachi's cold departure a year earlier and, urged by Sayaka's trust, reconciles with her to save the event, proving how far she's come in owning her place in the club.
103-14: Training for the Hokuriku Regionals, Kaho suggests performing as one six-member group to avoid units competing, but Kozue firmly refuses, valuing each unit's unique identity and her bond with Kaho in Cerise Bouquet. Then Sachi delivers grave news: a 'restricted' faction proposes an internet ban that would kill the club's School Idol Connect streaming. With Sachi's council term ending in December, Kaho proposes a gamble, perform the qualifier via remote stream and win using the very tech the school wants to ban, giving the permissive faculty leverage. The crisis deepens when a data cap and 'outing ban' block off-campus practice, forcing the club to fight for its existence.
103-15: After losing the Love Live! finals, Kaho wakes dazed in Kanazawa, struggling to process the defeat; Kozue notes this is the first real tournament loss the current members have felt. Kozue leads Kaho to check on everyone: Rurino feels like an imposter for joining late until Kozue validates her 'fun' motive; Megumi channels frustration into ruthless competitive resolve; Sayaka hides grief behind disciplined routine; and Tsuzuri sits melancholic on the roof until Kozue helps her name her sadness as pride in Hasunosora and a 'greedy' wish for the world to see it. Reunited, the six resolve not to let the loss define them.
103-16: Kaho realizes she never thanked the community that supported them (especially the TezaLink! Live) and rushes to propose a Special Thanks concert, discovering the others already planned the same. To prove her growth to Kozue, she volunteers to write Cerise Bouquet's new lyrics alone, but is paralyzed by writer's block. Sachi rescues her by inviting her to hand-deliver invitations to local Kanazawa fans, where Kaho learns the townspeople saw the loss not as failure but as a gift the club gave the city, refilling her resolve to write from the heart.
103-17: Rurino's low-energy 'battery drain' livestream shows her some fans find comfort in quiet moments, inspiring Valentine's ideas for tired people; Megumi counters with flashy 'sparkling cake' concepts, dismissing Rurino's 'vinegar kelp' ideas and her shorter tenure. Their clash over idol philosophy sparks a fight, so Rurino proposes a 'shuffle unit' showcase. The lots pair Kaho with Megumi, Kozue with Sayaka, and Rurino with Tsuzuri; while the other pairs sync instantly, Rurino learns to blend her fun-first energy with Tsuzuri's eccentric calm, reaffirming their equal partnership and that the club makes room for both dreams.
103-18: As Sachi's graduation nears, the second-years, Kozue, Tsuzuri, and Megumi, resolve to gift her a brand-new song for the Renge Festival, dividing roles (song, dance, words) and pulling juniors in. Kozue invites Kaho to her estate, reflecting on how Sachi turned her from a rigid loner into a collaborator; Tsuzuri, walked through Kanazawa by Sayaka, embraces her place among friends; and Megumi, with Rurino, faces her 'black history' first stream and credits Sachi for a new dream. Recalling their disastrous 102nd-term first meeting, the trio thanks Sachi for holding them together and delivers the song as a heartfelt farewell to their senior.
104-1: The new school year opens with Kaho oversleeping and rushing in, delighted to find Sayaka and Rurino in her same class as second-years; self-conscious she hasn't 'grown up,' she adopts a stiff formal speech to look like a mature senior, amusing her friends. As upperclassmen they discuss recruiting freshmen and their units' differing philosophies, Sayaka noting DOLLCHESTRA won't chase recruits, but a quiet first-year, Ginko Momose, is already lingering near the club room absorbing its 'tradition,' and when Kaho clumsily serves tea and Ginko's notebook spills to reveal dozens of original costume designs, Kaho impulsively invites her to join Cerise Bouquet, setting the recruitment season in motion.
104-2: The seniors show effortless synergy in practice, impressing first-years Ginko, Kosuzu, and Hime, and Kozue announces the club's invitation to headline the Tsuruga School Idol Live Festa, until a conflict emerges: the third-years will be on their Tokyo school trip during it, leaving the underclassmen to perform alone. Kaho initially panics at the responsibility, but the juniors' determination and the seniors' trust push her to accept leading the show, marking the first time the new generation carries the club's name without their mentors on stage.
104-3: Kaho, Sayaka, and Rurino game together and reminisce about last year's Nadeshiko Festival, where Sayaka notes first-years get the most leadership chances and must write the club article, Kaho comically fears a low 'rating' from Ginko. Megumi reveals the club will perform a joint live plus unit exhibits, and as the underclassmen prepare to lead, they begin understanding mentorship from the other side, with Rurino reassuring the seniors they're doing fine even as the third-years' trip looms.
104-4: Kaho, Kozue, and Ginko inventory the storage warehouse, where Kaho finds old Performing Arts Club costumes and they discuss preserving the club's legacy; Ginko admits she finds Kaho's physical closeness and high energy hard to handle, keeping distance to maintain decorum as a junior. Kozue shows Ginko that Kaho devised the inspiring 'Umbrella Sky' live that drew Ginko to the school, deepening Ginko's respect for her senior even as she struggles to manage Kaho's exuberance.
104-5: Kosuzu films a 'history of successful challenges' video but is clearly overexerting herself; found asleep in the clubroom, she reveals a letter from her childhood friend Sekka, who taught her the value of challenges and whom she idolizes, explaining her drive to prove herself. The club worries she's pushing too hard alone, and Tsuzuri relates to her fear of being late, but Sayaka discourages the sleep-in habit, gently reminding Kosuzu she doesn't have to carry everything by herself.
104-6: Hime, inspired by Mira-Cra Park! but slumping badly in her online game (a ten-game losing streak bleeding into practice), is cheered by Megumi's high energy and Rurino's reminder that both gaming and idols are team efforts where they support each other. They encourage her to use practice to wash away frustration and focus on joy, and Hime begins rebuilding confidence by leaning on her unit rather than isolating over the losses.
104-7: The club meets to plan the Rindou Festival and Love Live! qualifiers, this year entering as one collective unit merging all three; Sayaka and Rurino lead, with Megumi nudging Rurino to speak up. They choose 'Link to the FUTURE,' the song they lost the national finals with last year, as a deliberate move from past to future, and Ginko's concern about its history is reframed as the point: this time they perform it whole, as one club, turning a painful memory into their forward step.
104-8: The club celebrates passing the Love Live! district qualifiers, with Tsuzuri noting she's never had more fun now that she focuses on her friends over clouds. But the dorm mother reveals the room next to Tsuzuri's was vacated by early graduation, shaking Tsuzuri with the reality that members leave, and back in the buried-in-paperwork clubroom, Sayaka is overwhelmed until Kaho and Kosuzu help, showing the underclassmen stepping up to carry administrative load their seniors once bore.
104-9: The club celebrates Megumi clearing her grade after Kozue's immense tutoring effort, Rurino relieved Megumi won't be left behind at graduation; Hime jokes Megumi should fail two more years to stay. Megumi reflects that she entered feeling 'trapped in a prison' but triumphed doing exactly what she wanted, idols, editing, streaming, without yielding to the strict system, and when Ginko asks her future, Megumi's answer hints at how much she's grown from the arrogant star she was.
104-10: Kaho and Ginko visit Mizukawa Girls' School after Ceras's challenge; Ginko wants to gauge top-ranked Izumi Katsuragi to keep Hasunosora competitive. Ceras tours Kaho and opens up: a former violinist sidelined by illness, she was inspired by Mizukawa's idol club visiting her hospital with the message that anyone can start a dream anytime, and now aims to become a school idol there. At the stage, Ginko asks Izumi her motivation and gets a blunt answer that foreshadows the transfer to come.
104-11: A flashback shows Ceras scouting ~300 schools to save Mizukawa from closure and recruiting inexperienced Izumi through sheer passion, pledging herself to the cause. In the present, as Hasunosora preps the playoff, Ceras and Izumi deliver devastating news: Mizukawa's closure is finalized and club activities are suspended, forcing their withdrawal from Love Live!. The Hasunosora members mourn their rivals' loss even amid their own momentum, setting up Ceras and Izumi's search for a new home.
104-12: Back at Hasunosora after their Love Live! victory, Kozue is congratulated by peers and reflects it still feels like a dream; at a meeting led by Megumi, Kozue proposes Renge-sai as the graduation performance where each unit writes a culminating original song for the 104th term. Tsuzuri wants a song that stays in members' hearts forever, and Kozue praises everyone's growth. Later, the third-years begin shaping their final gifts to the club, even as Kaho travels exhaustedly to thank every supporter in person.
104-13: The third-years review their final songs under the cherry blossoms, reflecting on three years and Sachi's legacy, and back Sayaka as next president; they resolve to give their absolute best as a graduation gift. Meanwhile Kaho, Sayaka, and Rurino build a graduation album, Kaho overwhelmed narrowing photos until Sayaka reminds her static images evoke memories video can't. The first-years join, and the whole club collaborates on a farewell project, capturing how the generation that once struggled to stay together will send off its seniors with love.
105-1: Ceras mourns Mizukawa's closure with junior Kairi, promising its spirit lives on, yet arrives at Hasunosora brimming with excitement for a 'new world'; Izumi reveals she transferred to stand where she was defeated in last year's finals, hungry for that passion. The newcomers tour the bustling campus, Izumi adopting formal speech to honor the upperclassmen before relaxing into rapport as Kaho cheerfully calls her 'Izumi-chan,' and they begin the 105th term as outsiders carrying another school's legacy into Hasunosora's post-Love-Live dream.
105-2: Ceras playfully teases Ginko while the club wraps up its day; Kosuzu reflects the newcomers aren't replacements but bring their own 'colors,' and Ginko, embracing her second-year role, admits she finds Izumi and Ceras genuinely cute. Talk turns to Kaho's grand dream of a 'stage where everyone can bloom,' Kosuzu thrilled, but Hime privately worries her own gaming-and-idols dream is just 'hitching a ride' on Kaho's, seeding her internal conflict about belonging.
105-3: After the school trip, Sayaka tells Kaho she's clearing her schedule for Kaho's spontaneous ideas; Kaho reveals her 'Kaho-Hime Meeting' plan, a time-unrestricted live stage achieved by entering and winning a prestigious Rock Festival for year-long venue priority. Sayaka worries they're rock novices against professionals, but Kaho brings it to the club as the concrete path to her blooming-stage dream, challenging everyone to grow beyond their comfort zones.
105-4: As the seniors coordinate schedules and permissions, the underclassmen, Ginko, Kosuzu, and Hime, feel a widening gap and form the 'Hasu no Shousankaku' (Little Triangle) to host their own event and claim identity beyond the legendary seniors. Hime proposes a gaming booth, Ginko a fashion/embroidery booth, and they arrange booths in a triangle, asserting the juniors can shine on their own while still part of the whole club.
105-5: Ceras arrives early but finds Izumi already there; they review homework, a new Edel Note song for Fes×LIVE. Izumi has three polished demos, but Ceras rejects them as technically excellent yet lacking Izumi's personal identity, noting Izumi spent a year refining a 'standard' to help Ceras and stopped putting her own raw emotion in. Ceras shares her cathartic 'Death to Cicadas' vent song, pushing Izumi to write from herself, not just to please, reigniting Izumi's authentic voice.
105-6: Ginko's grandmother reports locals now ask for Ginko's autograph, calling the club the 'Stars of Kanazawa,' moved by their revitalization efforts, but notes older supporters don't know how to engage with streams or digital fandom. Ginko realizes a gap between the club and the community it represents, and the members, including Edel Note's Izumi and Ceras, brainstorm ways to welcome non-digital supporters, deepening the term's theme of blooming for everyone, not just online fans.
105-7: Sayaka reveals she'll attend university and continue figure skating, while Kaho stays undecided and Rurino doubts she truly wants Megumi's 'dazzle the world' path; Sayaka chides them it's already October of their third year. She then finds Kosuzu depressed, feeling left behind as peers gain clear goals, and Kosuzu even begs Sayaka to choose her career for her, forcing Sayaka to realize how much the juniors still lean on her guidance as graduation nears.
105-8: With the third-years busy prepping Starring Bloom, Izumi suggests Edel Note join the underclassmen for a 'special lesson' for Ceras before Edel Note disbands year-end; Kosuzu teaches 'freshly cooked rice' energy, Hime Mira-Cra fan service, Ginko strict conditioning. Ceras is overwhelmed but beloved, and Hime notes Izumi seems happier and more relaxed at Hasunosora than at Mizukawa, showing the transfer was healing for both of them.
105-9: Kaho, Sayaka, and Rurino announce the 102nd-gen trio, Kozue, Tsuzuri, and Megumi, will return for the March Bloom Garden Party, thrilling Kosuzu and Hime. Updates on the grads pour in (Tsuzuri's university dance circle, Kozue's lead role, Megumi's abroad videos), and Ceras shares Mizukawa's former students want to return to the stage after seeing the platform, proving the blooming spirit spreads beyond one school.
105-10: Drowning in Bloom Garden Party paperwork, the club is rocked when Hime reveals Megumi's first post-grad original MV, 'Halo-Megu Sanka,' already passed 100 million views globally. Rurino feels pressure and self-doubt about keeping pace with Megumi's 'enchant the world' heights, but Kaho and Sayaka quickly reassure her that her own path with Mira-Cra Park! is valid, turning awe into renewed resolve.
105-11: A flashback shows Kaho was named for being 'loved by many like a flower'; now she leads the national 'Bloom Garden Party Union' of groups inspired by Starring Bloom, writing a resource manual from their experience. Sayaka and Rurino take over the paperwork so Kaho can rest, and Sayaka reflects she's grown less willing to give up on others' dreams, capturing how far the once-struggling club has come in lifting people up.
105-12: As Kaho's fourth spring nears, the graduated trio returns for the Bloom Garden Party; Kozue hesitates at entering as an alumna but Kaho insists it's natural, and Tsuzuri's rare public hug flusters Sayaka as they reunite physically, not just in spirit. The whole club, seniors, graduates, and the Hasu no Shousankaku (Little Triangle), gathers to send off the 105th term with a celebration of every bloom they helped open, closing the story on connection across generations.
102-8: The day after their successful Nadeshiko Festival performance, the trio celebrates with senior Sachi in the clubroom over their favorite drinks, their bond now effortless while Kozue still flusters using first names. Sachi expresses pride in the concert and a quiet wish to someday perform alongside them as a full four-member group, and reveals the student body has already nicknamed them the 'Hasu no Daisankaku' (Great Triangle): three first-magnitude stars (Kozue the musical elite, Tsuzuri the dance prodigy, Megumi the former star) whose combined light defines the 102nd term.
dream-1: In March of their final term, Kaho proposes the three of them write a Sanrenka song together, inspired by Megumi's Asterism. Sayaka and Rurino agree, and each drafts lyrics independently, but every attempt fails: Kaho's fantasy epic is overblown, Sayaka's confessional too self-deprecating, and Rurino's version too fictionalized. Stuck, they film interview videos asking the club what Sanrenka means to them. Izumi, Ceras, Ginko, Kosuzu, and Hime each share their perspectives, yet the trio still cannot find their answer. Then Kaho scrolls through their group chat, the 'Hasu no Sanrenka' thread that holds three years of daily conversations. Looking back at Sayaka's absurdly formal first message, Rurino's random stamps, and Kaho's endless photo stream, they realize the answer was always there: not a grand myth, but the simple miracle that three very different people stayed by each other's side through everything. With this clarity, they write 'Perennial' and introduce it at the Bloom Garden Party as their finale.
dream-2: With Bloom Garden Party prep in full swing, Izumi asks Ceras which unit she will join next year after Edel Note disbands. Every unit welcomes her, but the pressure overwhelms Ceras and she declares she will go solo. Kosuzu, Hime, Ginko, and Izumi try to draw out her true feelings, but Ceras deflects everything. Kosuzu invokes the Big Voice Championship, where anyone can speak what they cannot say. Each member bares her heart: Kosuzu wants Ceras in DOLLCHESTRA, Hime in Mira-Cra Park!, Ginko in Cerise Bouquet, and Izumi offers unconditional support. Yet Ceras still insists on solo, until forced to admit she loves every unit so much she cannot choose, because the one she does not pick will be left alone. Reassured they will be fine on their own, Ceras finally asks Kosuzu to let her into DOLLCHESTRA, vowing to support her and build a new DOLLCHESTRA together. The two embrace in tears as the club celebrates.
dream-3: In the lead-up to the Hasu no Shousankaku (Little Triangle)'s first-ever joint live, Izumi gathers Ginko, Kosuzu, and Hime to choose a song that captures how the unit has leveled up now that she has joined as Hasu no Shoshihenkei (Little Rectangle). Rather than simply state her wish, the normally formal Izumi works behind the scenes, approaching each member one by one to quietly build consensus, earning teasing from the others who suspect she has an ulterior motive. When pressed, Izumi finally admits the truth she had been too ashamed to say: her only real desire was to stand on stage together with them as equals, and she has simply never been good at voicing what she wants. Throwing away that embarrassment, she asks the trio to perform the song with her, and the four of them pledge to make their debut Shoushihenkei live a soaring success.
